description: Authentication mechanisms including JWT, OAuth 2.0, SAML, session management, and authentication best practices

questions.question: What is JWT (JSON Web Token) and how does it work?
questions.answer: JWT is compact, URL-safe token for transmitting information between parties as JSON object. Structure: Header.Payload.Signature. Header contains algorithm (HS256, RS256), Payload contains claims (user data, expiration), Signature verifies integrity. Example: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJ1c2VyMTIzIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvaG4iLCJleHAiOjE2ODI5Nzc2MDB9.SflKxwRJSMeKKF2QT4fwpMeJf36POk6yJV_adQssw5c. Claims: sub (subject/user ID), exp (expiration), iat (issued at), iss (issuer). Stateless - server doesn't store session. Workflow: 1) User logs in with credentials, 2) Server validates, creates JWT with user info, 3) Client stores JWT (localStorage, httpOnly cookie), 4) Client sends JWT in Authorization header for requests, 5) Server verifies signature and expiration. Benefits: stateless, scalable, cross-domain. Risks: token theft (use HTTPS, short expiration), can't revoke before expiration (use refresh tokens or blacklist).

questions.question: Explain OAuth 2.0 flow and its grant types.
questions.answer: OAuth 2.0 is authorization framework enabling third-party access without sharing credentials. Roles: Resource Owner (user), Client (app), Authorization Server (issues tokens), Resource Server (API). Grant types: 1) Authorization Code - most secure, for server-side apps (user redirected to auth server, returns code, app exchanges code for token), 2) Implicit - for browser apps (deprecated, use PKCE), 3) Client Credentials - service-to-service (app credentials for token), 4) Password - user provides credentials directly (legacy). Example Authorization Code flow: User clicks 'Login with Google' → Redirected to Google → Approves → Google redirects to app with code → App sends code to Google token endpoint → Receives access token → Uses token to call Google APIs. Access token: short-lived (1 hour), Refresh token: long-lived, exchanges for new access token. PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) adds security for public clients. Spring Security OAuth2 supports all flows.
